message.content:
**Kill Visual Studio Code (code.exe) from the Windows command line**

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM code.exe` – matches the image name of the VS Code process.  
* `/F` – forces the termination (no graceful shutdown).

---

### If you want to kill *all* VS Code instances and their child processes

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

* `/T` – terminates the specified process **and** any child processes it has spawned.

---

### Using PowerShell

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or, to kill by PID:

```powershell
$pid = (Get-Process code).Id
Stop-Process -Id $pid -Force
```

---

### Quick sanity check

Before killing, you can list the running VS Code processes:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

This shows the PID(s) so you can confirm which instance(s) will be terminated.

---

**Tip:** If you’re scripting or automating, you can capture the output of `tasklist` or `Get-Process` to decide whether to kill or not.
